title: Retained detector outcomes can break memory equivalence despite matching test rates
statement: For resource/bath state (Phi+_RB|0>_M+Phi-_RB|1>_M)/sqrt(2), a ZZ parity test always passes. Retaining the individual00/11 detector outcomes steers the bath to |+>/|->; its flagged bath state differs from the Bell-pinched comparator by half trace distance1/2. Retiring the fine record and destructive carriers leaves the same coarse bath update. Separately, an untrusted terminal X can turn intended |0> into orthogonal |1> after a perfect upstream resource test.

requires: The specified coherent Bell/bath witness and actual retention of separate fine outcomes for the flagged comparison; only coarse parity after retirement for the equality case.
The terminal counterexample puts an unconstrained X after all upstream testing; no bound on that terminal map is assumed.
provides: For resource/bath state (Phi+_RB|0>_M+Phi-_RB|1>_M)/sqrt(2), a ZZ parity test always passes. assumptions: This is not a claim that all fine measurements or all trusted terminal operations fail; their full instruments may be separately bounded.
Discarding a displayed record while allowing a correlated copy or fine-controlled future action is not the required physical retirement.
costs: Charge protected storage, complete record retirement and trusted/independently bounded terminal gates; upstream sampling cannot remove these costs.
contract.units: Half trace distance and outcome probabilities are dimensionless; the example uses one bath qubit and a two-qubit resource.
contract.obstruction: Supply the actual retained-record and final-output interface before reusing a coarse upstream certificate.

body: Expand the resource in the00 and11 local outcomes. Each occurs with probability1/2 and leaves a pure bath |+> or |->. The Bell-pinched reference leaves I/2 in either flagged branch. Each flag block contributes1/4 to half trace distance, totaling1/2, even though the coarse parity failure effect is zero in both cases. Forgetting the fine flag sums the opposite coherences to zero and restores the coarse update. Equal effects/pass statistics therefore do not authorize a complete-memory instrument substitution with extra accessible records. The output-X witness is independent: no operation that occurred before the untrusted X can test that later action. Retired-record equivalence must concern the actual complete set of future-used registers and controls, not merely a decision to omit them from a log. Keeping the unknown payload isolated until post-call acceptance keeps its logical wire out of the earlier physical call; it does not certify a conditional joint state or the later Bell measurement/correction/output boundary.
